title: Measurement-Invariance Translator
summary: Set the loadings, intercepts and latent means for two fictional groups, and manufacture an observed difference while the true difference stays at zero. Configural, metric and scalar invariance appear as pictures first.
learningObjectives: Recognise a loading difference and an intercept difference from a graph of item behaviour.
State what configural, metric and scalar invariance each licence you to compare.
Explain why an observed mean difference is not yet a finding about people.
Explain how an item such as speaking up in a group can be harder to endorse at the same level of the trait.
Report which invariance level was reached and confine claims to what it supports.
interactionTypes: multi-select challenge scored against current settings
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every calculation runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native ranges, checkboxes, radios and buttons throughout; every slider announces what it controls in words ('how readily this item is endorsed at an average level of the trait'). Each item's parameter group is a fieldset whose floated legend carries the item text, so sliders are never announced orphaned and multi-line legends do not spill out of their box. The item-behaviour panels are hidden from assistive technology and paired with a visible table giving every loading and intercept and stating in words whether the slope, the level or both differ. The invariance ladder states each level in plain language first, gives its status as the word 'Holds' or 'Does not hold', and names the technical term second. Reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Measurement invariance: what configural, metric and scalar each licence, and how an item can manufacture a group difference
simulationNotes: Two fictional groups with no nationality, ethnicity, language, region or culture, and four original items written for this tool. Item means are intercept plus loading times latent mean; invariance levels are read directly from the parameters with a tolerance rather than by fitting a model. No fit index, chi-square or p-value is produced, deliberately, because inventing one would teach students to expect a number where real invariance testing gives a judgement built from nested model comparison. Partial invariance is not modelled. Where the tool discusses why an item might behave differently it refers to a setting - whether disagreeing openly is invited or costly - and never to a people.
